visual_elements.description: Confusion matrix for Threshold=0.0. Headers: 'Predicted as' above columns P and N. Row header 'Actual' with rows P and N. Cells: P row: 5 (red), 0 (black); N row: 6 (black), 0 (red). To the right: 'TPR=5/(5+0)=1' and 'FPR=6/(6+0)=1'.

Confusion matrix for Threshold=0.1. Headers: 'Predicted as' above columns P and N. Row header 'Actual' with rows P and N. Cells: P row: 5 (red), 0 (black); N row: 4 (black), 2 (red). To the right: 'TPR=5/(5+0)=1' and 'FPR=4/(4+2)=0.66'.

Confusion matrix for Threshold=0.3. Headers: 'Predicted as' above columns P and N. Row header 'Actual' with rows P and N. Cells: P row: 5 (red), 0 (black); N row: 2 (black), 4 (red). To the right: 'TPR=5/(5+0)=1' and 'FPR=2/(2+4)=0.33'.

ROC curve plot. Y-axis labeled 'TPR' (vertical text). X-axis labeled 'FPR' (horizontal text). Light blue plot area with grid. Three data points marked with red circles, labeled above with '0.3' (left), '0.1' (center), '0.0' (right). Blue border around plot area.
Text box containing two equations: 'TPR = TP / TP + FN' and 'FPR = FP / FP + TN'. Red border.
Small confusion matrix legend. Headers: 'Predicted as' above columns P and N. Row header 'Actual' with rows P and N. Cells: P,P = TP (red); P,N = FN (black); N,P = FP (black); N,N = TN (green).

recreation_brief:
1. Set the slide background to white (#FFFFFF).
2. Place the slide number "31" as black text inside a yellow (#FFFF00) circle in the top-right corner (approximately 5% from the top and right edges).
3. Draw a vertical blue (#0000FF) divider line separating the left column from the center and right areas.
4. Create a red-bordered panel in the top-left (approximately 25% width, 20% height). Add the bold header "Threshold=0.0". Insert a 2x2 confusion matrix table with the top header "Predicted as" spanning columns P and N, and the left header "Actual" spanning rows P and N. Fill the cells: row P / col P = 5 in red (#FF0000); row P / col N = 0 in black (#000000); row N / col P = 6 in black (#000000); row N / col N = 0 in red (#FF0000). To the right of the table, add the text "TPR=5/(5+0)=1" and "FPR=6/(6+0)=1" in black.
5. Create a red-bordered panel in the middle-left (approximately 25% width, 20% height). Add the bold header "Threshold=0.1". Insert an identical 2x2 confusion matrix table. Fill the cells: row P / col P = 5 in red; row P / col N = 0 in black; row N / col P = 4 in black; row N / col N = 2 in red. To the right, add "TPR=5/(5+0)=1" and "FPR=4/(4+2)=0.66".
6. Create a red-bordered panel in the bottom-left (approximately 25% width, 20% height). Add the bold header "Threshold=0.3". Insert an identical 2x2 confusion matrix table. Fill the cells: row P / col P = 5 in red; row P / col N = 0 in black; row N / col P = 2 in black; row N / col N = 4 in red. To the right, add "TPR=5/(5+0)=1" and "FPR=2/(2+4)=0.33".
7. Place a box at the bottom-center (approximately 30% width, 10% height) containing the text "ROC Curve for Same Model -different thresholds".
8. Create a blue-bordered graph area in the top-right (approximately 35% width, 55% height) with a light blue (#ADD8E6) plot background and grid lines. Label the Y-axis "TPR" using vertical text and the X-axis "FPR" using horizontal text. Plot three data points as red (#FF0000) circles: place the left point with the label "0.3" above it, the center point with the label "0.1" above it, and the right point with the label "0.0" above it.
9. Create a red-bordered formula panel in the bottom-right left side (approximately 35% width, 20% height). Add two lines of black text: "TPR = TP / TP + FN" and "FPR = FP / FP + TN".
10. To the right of the formula panel, create a small 2x2 confusion matrix legend table with the top header "Predicted as" spanning columns P and N, and the left header "Actual" spanning rows P and N. Fill the cells: TP in red (#FF0000); FN in black (#000000); FP in black (#000000); TN in green (#00FF00).
